author: BaldwinBravo
text_post: In the Trivial Everyday Misandry thread, I described an experience I had many years ago that I have wanted to re create with a camera present ever since. (The post was lengthy, so I will not repeat it here, but it can be found on this page: http://forums.avoiceformen.com/showthread.php?tid=482&pid=8304#pid8304 ) In a nutshell, the experience was that while struggling to get around on a crutch and with a broken arm, 100% of people who gave me assistance were male; teenagers and seniors notwithstanding. To be clear, I do not believe that this is the natural state of women, rather the effects of socialization. I believe that the results would be very different in a small rural town. I would propose, if I can find volunteers in the Toronto area to help out, to get a fake cast and a crutch, and film people as they either hold open doors, or fail to do so. We would perform this experiment a number of times, first to get some numbers, then repeated adding short interviews with subjects who are willing, presenting them with the results of the previous test. Thirdly, we would repeat the experiment in a rural town (this would require a road trip... who doesn't like a road trip, though ) Fourth, I would propose using a female on the crutch, to see if that has any effect. Naturally, this could not be considered a scientific study, as there are far too many variables to control, however, if a decent video could be produced and made public, it would at very least get people thinking about compassion for others, and ideally make the world a slightly better place to be. Is there anyone in the Toronto area who would be interested in doing this in the spring? (it would have to be in the spring, we couldn't have the cast covered up with a winter coat) It would also be awesome if people in other cities would do similar experiments... but baby steps

author: Prince_Tybalt
text_post: RE: A social experiment on compassion Arguable, though I've highlighted similar sentiments in my life.   Recently a buddy of mine and I were working out at a playground (they're great places for exercise).  A woman came with a young girl, and she sat and was chatting on her cell phone a fair distance away while the little girl (3-5 years old) came and played on the playground with us.   We were both kind of cautious at first, but I kept interacting with her, since the woman wasn't staying close to her and playgrounds can also be a good place to get injured.  The girl was running up and down and yelling for us to watch her go down the slide.  She would yell out "CATCH ME!!!", and I'd wait for her, but let her land on her own to show her she didn't need me as a safety net.  The woman (I believe she was an aunt) didn't seem to mind, but then she was talking with another couple who was asking who we were, and I felt they were more concerned with the 2 grown men at the playground than she had been. To be fair, I'd likely question 2 adults without a kid(s) at a playground too.
